subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Volkswagen Beetle
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Volkswagen Beetle usable.

hook.text: A car designed under Nazi Germany became the best-selling vehicle of the 20th century.

buildup.text: Ferdinand Porsche designed the Beetle in the 1930s as a 'people's car'—cheap, simple, air-cooled.

discovery.text: After the war, the British Army restarted the Wolfsburg factory and the Beetle went global.

twist.text: In America, the tiny Beetle was the anti-Detroit car—small, honest, and rebellious.

climax.text: Over 21 million were built. The Beetle outlasted every competitor from its era.

punchline.text: The people's car outlived the regime that created it.

quiz.question: Who designed the original Volkswagen Beetle?

details.summary: The Volkswagen Beetle, designed by Ferdinand Porsche for Nazi Germany's people's car program, became an unlikely icon of peace and counterculture, selling over 21 million units worldwide.
details.whyItMatters: The Beetle proved that simple, affordable, and reliable design could create global success. Its cultural impact transcended transportation, becoming a symbol of freedom and individuality.
takeaways: Ferdinand Porsche designed it as Hitler's Kraft durch Freude car
Over 21 million original Beetles were produced from 1938 to 2003
It surpassed the Model T as the best-selling car in history

faq.question: How did a car designed for the Nazis become a peace symbol?
faq.answer: After the war, British forces restarted Beetle production to rebuild Germany's economy. Its cheerful shape, affordability, and clever marketing by DDB made it beloved by the 1960s counterculture generation.

faq.question: Was the Beetle a good car technically?
faq.answer: It was simple, air-cooled, and extremely reliable. It lacked power and modern safety features, but its toughness and ease of repair made it ideal for buyers worldwide who valued dependability over performance.
